newsitem.title: USA: Clinton to make cost of living announcement soon.
newsitem.headline: Clinton to make cost of living announcement soon.

text.p: President Bill Clinton said on Wednesday he would make an announcement soon on what procedure should be adopted to reform the way cost of living changes are measured.

"I will have some sort of announcement on that in the not too distant future," Clinton said in response to a reporter's question at a joint news conference with visiting Chilean President Eduardo Frei.
Clinton said Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott's proposal Monday to create a commission to decide how to correct any bias in the Consumer Price Index would be one option under consideration.

"I think (Lott) made a good constructive suggestion; I think we ought to take that under advisement, and I think we ought to see what other options there are out there," he said. "We need to go forward. And I expect to do that," he added.
Gene Sperling, Chairman of the White House National Economic Council, said later that Clinton would make the announcment in the next few weeks.
Clinton said he was in favor of having a system that was accurate, but he said any changes must have credibility.

"I think it's important that we agree to a procedure that will have credibility, not only among both parties and their leaders in Congress, but even more importantly out there among the American people," Clinton said.
A blue-ribbon commission headed by Stanford University economist Michael Boskin has said the current CPI measure overstates inflation by about one percentage point per year.
A lower CPI measure would save the government millions of dollars in cost-of-living-adjusted benefit payments.
